questions.question: The essential difference between a wage and a salary is:
options: The UNIT of payment — the hour for the wage, the year for the salary
The importance of the job
Wages are taxed; salaries are not
Salaries are always larger than wages

questions.question: In the scale R96 000 × R9 600 — R144 000, the middle figure is:
options: The monthly salary
The annual increment — the notch increase added each year of service
The maximum overtime allowed
The employer's contribution

questions.question: How many increments does it take to climb that scale from bottom to top?
options: Six — one for each year including the first
Four — R48 000 divided by R12 000
Five — the distance of R48 000 divided by the notch of R9 600
Ten — R96 000 divided by R9 600

questions.question: An employee in her second year on that scale earns per month:
options: R8 800 — the annual R105 600 divided by twelve

subtopics.title: Normal Time and the Overtime Multipliers

questions.question: With a normal rate of R40 per hour, the time-and-a-half and double-time rates are:
options: R60 and R80
R45 and R50
R50 and R60
R80 and R120

questions.question: Double time typically applies to:
options: Any hour after 17:00
Sundays and public holidays
The first five hours of any overtime
Every hour in a busy week

questions.question: The calculation discipline the marking rewards is:
options: Compute the final total first, then check it
Multiply all hours by the normal rate, then adjust
Derive each overtime RATE as its own labelled line before multiplying by the hours
Estimate the overtime and round at the end

questions.question: GROSS pay is:
options: What the worker takes home after deductions
Only the overtime portion of the pay
The employer's total cost including contributions
What the work earned before a single cent is deducted

subtopics.title: A Week at Thabo's Trading — the Wage Run

questions.question: S. Dlamini: 45 normal hours at R40 plus 4 evening overtime hours. His gross is:
options: R2 040 — R1 800 normal plus 4 × R60
R1 800 — overtime is unpaid

questions.question: B. Mokoena: 45 hours at R36 plus 2 Sunday hours. Her Sunday rate and gross are:
options: R54 and R1 728
R72 and R1 764 — double time on R36; R1 620 plus R144
R36 and R1 692
R72 and R1 800

questions.question: If Dlamini's 4 overtime hours fell on a public holiday instead, his gross becomes:
options: R2 040 — the day makes no difference
R2 120 — the rate line changes to R80, the overtime line to R320

questions.question: The week's total gross wage bill (original scenario) is:

subtopics.title: The Salary Side and Exam Technique

questions.question: The administrator, in her second year of service on R96 000 × R9 600 — R144 000, now earns monthly:
options: R8 000 — she stays on the starting notch until the top
R9 600 — two notches for standing in year two
R8 800 — one COMPLETED year means one notch: R105 600 per year, divided by twelve
R12 000 — the ceiling divided by twelve

questions.question: The number of notches applied always equals:
options: The number of COMPLETED years of service
The year of service you are standing in
The employee's age minus 18
The months worked divided by six

questions.question: Annual salary converts to monthly pay by:
options: Dividing by 13 to allow for a bonus
Dividing by twelve, only at the END of the calculation
Dividing by the number of working days
Multiplying by the notch

questions.question: The wage earner's gross versus the salary earner's gross:
options: Both respond to the hours of the week
Both are fixed for the year
The salary responds weekly; the wage is fixed
The wage RESPONDS to the week's hours; the salary is STABLE with growth arriving through the annual notch

questions.question: "I sell my hours" and "I sell my year" describe:
options: The wage deal (counted by the clock) and the salary deal (one number sliced into twelve)
Overtime and normal time
Gross pay and net pay
The employer's and employee's views of the same pay

questions.question: Why does the "year deal" fit the office job better than the "clock deal"?
options: Office workers may not legally earn wages
The responsibility is continuous — the same in January as in June — so a stable slice fits
Salaries are cheaper for the shop
Office hours cannot be counted

questions.question: Both deals produce a number called GROSS, which is:
options: The take-home amount after deductions
The employer's profit on the worker
What the work earned before anything is taken off
The overtime portion only

questions.question: The three rows of the hourly price list (normal R40) are:
options: R40 plain; R60 evenings and Saturdays; R80 Sundays and public holidays
R40 weekdays; R40 Saturdays; R60 Sundays

questions.question: Unsocial hours are paid more because:
options: The work is physically harder at night
They cost the worker more to give — rest, weekends, family time
The shop earns more on Sundays
The law taxes them differently

questions.question: The one trap in wage calculations, and the habit that beats it:
options: Forgetting normal hours; count them twice to be safe
Rounding the rate; always round up
Multiplying overtime hours by the PLAIN price; beat it by writing the correct row's price BEFORE touching the hours
Adding gross twice; subtract once at the end

questions.question: Mokoena's two Sunday stocktake hours (normal rate R36) add to her gross:
options: R144 — two hours at the double price of R72

questions.question: On the ladder R96 000 × R9 600 — R144 000, each rung represents:
options: One completed year of service, worth R9 600 more per year
One month of work
A promotion to a new position
R9 600 of overtime

questions.question: The ladder "makes tomorrow visible" because:
options: It guarantees promotion
The worker can read exactly what year four pays before year one is finished — and the shop can budget years ahead
It hides future pay from the worker
It changes with each month's profits

questions.question: When the ladder tops out at R144 000, further rising comes only from:
options: Automatic yearly notches continuing forever
Overtime multipliers
A new ladder — a promotion to a different scale
Dividing by eleven instead of twelve

questions.question: The three moves for any ladder question are:
options: Guess the rung; check the answer; move on
Multiply by twelve; add the notch; subtract deductions
Count the hours; find the rate; multiply
Count completed years for the rung; divide by twelve for the month; measure the ladder and divide by the rung for the top
